img-bourg-la-reine.attribution: Postcard (after 1908) of La Grande-Rue, Bourg-la-Reine, showing the birthplace of Évariste Galois (the Villa Bourg-la-Reine, his grandfather's and father's house). Anonymous author. Public domain (PD-anon-70-EU). Wikimedia Commons.
img-bourg-la-reine.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons. Stands in for an early-19th-century view of the village (no 1820 image of the Grande-Rue is available on public-domain repositories).

img-cochin-hospital.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons and downscaled to 3000px max via `sips`. Stands in for the Hôpital Cochin façade — the building Galois was brought to after his duel; the 1930 photograph predates modernist additions and shows the same 18th-century structure.

img-galois-testament-p1.attribution: Évariste Galois, surviving page of the letter to Auguste Chevalier, 29 May 1832. Public domain (author died 1832). Wikimedia Commons.
img-galois-testament-p1.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons. Used as the opening reference of the testament. Only one page facsimile is available on public-domain repositories; the visualizer should display the upper portion to suggest 'opening' the letter.

img-galois-testament-p2.attribution: Évariste Galois, final page of letter to Auguste Chevalier, 29 May 1832 — the closing passage where Galois asks Jacobi or Gauss to opine publicly on the importance of the theorems. Public domain (author died 1832). Wikimedia Commons.
img-galois-testament-p2.method: Same Wikimedia source as testament-p1 (this IS the closing page). Visualizer should crop to the lower portion / signature area to emphasize the closing request to Jacobi and Gauss.

img-galois-testament-margin-jenaipaslete.method: Hand-coded SVG (project palette, dark navy bg, cream serif). Recreates the famous marginal annotation 'Je n'ai pas le temps.' (Galois used the period spelling 'Je n'ai pas le tems') as an iconic typographic moment. Substituted because no public-domain photographic facsimile of the specific marginal note from the Premier Mémoire is available on Wikimedia Commons; the manuscripts are held in dossier 2, Ms 2108, Bibliothèque de l'Institut de France, with reproductions only in modern critical editions (Bourgne–Azra 1962, Neumann 2011).

img-galois-cenotaph-bourg-la-reine.attribution: Photograph of the cenotaph of Évariste Galois at the cemetery of Bourg-la-Reine (on his father Nicolas-Gabriel Galois's tomb). November 2024. Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication. Wikimedia Commons.
img-galois-cenotaph-bourg-la-reine.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons and downscaled to 2400px tall via `sips`. (Galois himself was buried in a common grave at Montparnasse; only this cenotaph in his hometown is visitable.)

img-liouville-portrait.attribution: Portrait of Joseph Liouville (1809–1882). Photograph of a 19th-century portrait, Wikimedia Commons. Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International.
img-liouville-portrait.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons, original resolution preserved.

img-liouville-1846-cover.attribution: Title page of the inaugural volume (1836) of Joseph Liouville's 'Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées'. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain in France and the United States. Wikimedia Commons.
img-liouville-1846-cover.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons. Stands in for the 1846 volume (XI) in which Liouville published Galois's Œuvres mathématiques: Wikimedia hosts the inaugural-volume title page only; the journal's masthead and design were unchanged across the 1830s–40s, so this title page accurately conveys 'Liouville's journal' as an artefact.

img-jordan-1870-traite.attribution: Title page of Camille Jordan, 'Traité des substitutions et des équations algébriques', Gauthier-Villars, Paris, 1870 (winner of the 1870 Prix Poncelet). Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica (bpt6k290534, f1). Public domain (Jordan d. 1922; printed 1870).
img-jordan-1870-traite.method: Downloaded the medium-resolution facsimile of folio 1 (title page) from Gallica.

img-klein-portrait.attribution: Felix Klein (1849–1925), photographic portrait by Gebrüder Noelle, before 1897. Accademia delle Scienze di Torino, inv. 0078 B. Public domain (photographer d. 1917). Wikimedia Commons.
img-klein-portrait.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons, original resolution preserved.

img-noether-portrait.attribution: Emmy Noether (1882–1935), photographic portrait, anonymous, c. 1900–1910. Public domain (PD-anon-70-EU; PD-US-published-before-1929). Source: MAA / Flickr (5506847067) via Wikimedia Commons.
img-noether-portrait.method: Downloaded from Wikimedia Commons, original resolution preserved.

diag-cayley-table-s3.method: Hand-coded SVG (project palette: dark navy bg #0e1117, accents #58a6ff blue / #ffd866 yellow / #f97583 rose / #c792ea violet / #4a5160 slate). 6×6 Cayley table for the symmetric group S₃ ≅ D₃ presented as a colored multiplication grid with row & column headers (e, r, r², s, sr, sr²), color-coded cells indicating the product, an element legend on the right, and the defining relations r³ = e, s² = e, srs = r⁻¹. Used at line 252 of script.md as 'diag-cayley-table-s3' — the symmetries of the equation diagram.

img-mother-adelaide.method: Hand-coded SVG name card on dark navy bg (project palette). No portrait of Adélaïde-Marie Demante (1788–1872), Galois's mother, is known to survive — fabricating one would be irresponsible. The SVG is a typographic placeholder showing 'Adélaïde-Marie Demante · 1788 – 1872 · Évariste's mother' in the project's serif treatment, suitable as a brief beat-card before the narration moves on.
